issues.what: Egypt's 'wrong' keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1300 (-1300..-1241) carries Cliopatria's own Syria-reaching shape as its correction; the compiler reads it as a claim and, with the -1400 shape cut at -1353, snapped Egypt at -1300 to Syria north of Canaan (65 cells; kept for 1273..1241 too, although the dossier's keyframe -1275 holds Amurru and Kadesh for 1275-1274 only).
issues.result: Trial: the -1300 snap is gone; the -1275 keyframe adds the 65 Syrian cells for 1275-1274 (as the dossier intends) and the -1273 keyframe releases 59 of them (9 kept by others).

issues.what: The twin keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1240 (-1240..-1151) has the same defect. It is already overridden by m1200-m1101 keyframe_overrides/0 with Cliopatria's whole -1240 shape (-1240..-1201), and the compiler reads patch files in file-name order, so m1200-m1101 comes before m1300-m1201 and wins: an override written in m1300-m1201 is skipped ('keyframe already overridden by data/patches/m1200-m1101.json: keyframe_overrides/0', seen in a scratch trial).
issues.decision: left: cannot be patched from m1300-m1201; m1200-m1101 keyframe_overrides/0 must be corrected (see problems)
issues.result: With my -1300 override alone, the -1240 snap (m1200-m1101's whole shape) gives Egypt 59 direct Syrian and Transjordan cells again (25 more kept by others) from -1240 until the -1200 snap removes them; the m1200 end anchor is unchanged.

issues.what: Seam at -900: twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-900 (Cliopatria's whole Egypt outline, -900..-801 by shapes.csv, no 'to' although the dossier note holds it for -900..-838 only) snapped the state back to the outline at -900 (+759 cells: New Valley 525, Red Sea 180, Matruh 48; -48) after the m1000-m0901 override of the -943 keyframe ended at -901, and was unioned with the Lower Egypt keyframe at -837. Overridden with the Delta plus Nile valley plus Fayyum shape of the -943 override, from -900 to -838.
issues.result: Trial: no -900 snap; the m0900 anchor is identical to the published one; the dossier's own -837 Lower Egypt keyframe now trims 176 cells (Giza 98, Minya 29, Suez 18, +6) and adds 19, so the m0800 anchor has 381 fewer Twenty-second Dynasty cells (they were removed later by the m0800-m0701 snap of -800). New conflict row: kingdom-of-kush / twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt, 42 cells at -900, Kush wins (R2): the same Lower Nubia strip that m1000-m0901 rulings/1 and the R2 rule already give to Kush at -1000 and -943.

issues.what: Seam at -1000: the dossier keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1000 (whole outline) would add about 486 New Valley and Red Sea cells to Tanis as a snap; the Twenty-first Dynasty page does not mention the oases.
issues.result: Already decided by m1000-m0901 keyframe_overrides/0 (Lower Egypt minus Matruh, -1000..-944): no 21st-dynasty snap at -1000 in the published draft or keyframe_snaps.csv, the m1000 anchor holds 263 Twenty-first Dynasty plus 216 priests' cells and no oasis cells. The page confirms silence: 'mostly active only in Lower Egypt, which they controlled'; 'High Priests of Amun at Thebes effectively ruled Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name'; no oases, Western Desert or Red Sea. The Assyria remark of the report (97 cells at -1000) is not part of the Egyptian question and was not touched.

problems: FILE ORDER: the README and the brief say 'the first window in order wins' when two files override one shape, but compile_dossiers.patch_files sorts the file names as strings, so for the m (BCE) windows the later window comes first: m1200-m1101 before m1300-m1201, m1000-m0901 before m1100-m1001, and so on. Any seam item that needs an override in the earlier-starting window of a shape already overridden in a later-named file is silently skipped by the compile (my scratch trial shows it; --check-patch of one file does not).

NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR (m1200-m1101.json, which I may not touch): replace keyframe_overrides/0 (new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1240, adjust, -1240..-1201): {"correction": {"union": [{"cliopatria": "New Kingdom of Egypt", "year": -1500, "text": "Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape"}, {"region": "Canaan", "text": "Canaan"}], "text": "Egypt, Nubia and Canaan (vassal tint), the shape of keyframes -1352 and -1273, with no Syria north of Canaan"}} in place of its present correction (the whole Cliopatria -1240 shape); keep from -1240, to -1201 and the source. Tested in a scratch copy of the patches folder: the -1240 snap disappears, the -1273 snap releases 59 cells, and the m1200 end anchor then differs from the published one only by 47 Egyptian cells that become unowned.

m0800-m0701: its packet's -800 snap of twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt_-800 (published: removed 381) will shrink, because those desert cells are now released at -837 by the dossier's own Lower Egypt keyframe (m0800 anchor: 381 cells change from the Twenty-second Dynasty to nobody). No patch there is affected.
My m0900-m0801 keyframe_overrides/0 reaches -838, inside the window; nothing crosses a window boundary. The -1300 override keeps shapes.csv years (-1300..-1241), all inside m1300-m1201.

Observation, not patched: the gazetteer's 'Lower Egypt' (used by the m1100-m1001, m1000-m0901 and now m0900-m0801 corrections) includes a wing of the Giza governorate's western desert (about 98 cells, Bahariya side) drawn as Egyptian from -1077 to -838; the pages name no desert land for the Twenty-first or Twenty-second Dynasty. It disappears at -837 with the Lower Egypt keyframe. I kept the same spec as the neighbour windows so no snap is created.
